newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU to hold special meeting on postal services.
newsitem.headline: EU to hold special meeting on postal services.

text.p: European Union postal ministers will hold a special meeting on Wednesday to try to break a deadlock over how to open up EU postal services to more competition, EU officials said.
The meeting was scheduled after EU leaders ordered the ministers at a weekend summit meeting in Dublin to settle the issue before the end of the year.

EU governments are under pressure to act quickly because the European Commission has said it will outline by the end of the year how it plans to apply EU competition rules to the postal sector -- with or without an accord by ministers.
"Postal services form an essential component of the communications infrastructure in the Union," the leaders said in a statement.
But EU diplomats in Brussels said they were not sure what kind of initiative would be taken to find a compromise. "Everybody I've talked to about this is pretty vague," one said.

Postal ministers were unable at a meeting in November to bridge the gap between a Franco-German camp that wanted to delay signficant liberalisation until at least 2003 and an Anglo-Nordic camp that wanted a quicker timetable.
The main question involves when to abolish state postal monopolies over direct mail and cross-border mail.
France, wary of inciting further public unrest, refuses to accept any plan that calls for automatic liberalisation of those sectors.
It has won support from Germany, which despite plans to liberalise its own postal sector has agreed to back France out of solidarity.
But their stance was rejected by a blocking minority of Austria, Britain, Denmark, Finland, the Netherlands and Sweden.

The Commission, under pressure from the direct mail industry, express operators and others to chip away at state monopolies, argues that post offices must become more competitive in an era of electronic mail and faxes.

Industry Commissioner Martin Bangemann said after the November meeting that the Commission was obliged under the EU treaty to respond to complaints about unfair competition in the sector. -- Brussels Newsroom 32 2 287 6800
